# Code Map — Backend

One shared .NET API: one class library per domain, composed in the Api gateway. Every
domain library has the same shape — Domain/ (aggregates), Application/ (vertical use-case
slices), Infrastructure/ (DI root, Endpoints/, Persistence/).

**Migrations: DO NOT READ files under Infrastructure/Persistence/Migrations/ — generated 1,600–2,000-line Designer files. The map records count + latest name only.**

- Kernel/Roles.cs is the only source of role strings (case-sensitive, ordinal matching) — never string literals.
- Messaging/Sender.cs is the hand-rolled mediator (no MediatR). EventBus: delivery is outbox polling (OutboxPollingConsumer); RabbitMQ carries only BusPublicationRegistry entries — first live entry (constructed in SharedServiceCollectionExtensions.cs): booking.booking-day-confirmed → Trips.
- RabbitMqIntegrationEventConsumer pushes AmbientTenant from the event's TenantId payload BEFORE resolving the handler scope — ModuleDbContext captures the tenant at construction, so a scope built earlier would silently filter out every row.
- HoursOfService/ is the pure HOS rule engine (Manitoba M.R. 72/2007, Cycle 1 only; no clock, no I/O — README.md beside it is the purity contract and regulation map). Dispatcher/lib/hos/engine.ts is its line-for-line TS mirror (DriverField re-copies it), held to it by the shared hos-fixtures.json in Backend/tests/NorthernLink.Shared.Tests/HoursOfService; HosWire owns every HOS wire string.
<!-- notes:shared:end -->

<!-- notes:trips:start -->
- Domain/Trips/Trip.cs owns the billing-driven lifecycle: ReadyForBilling → Invoiced → Completed (Completed means paid); CloseWithoutBilling is the write-off path; Reopen (below) is the only way backwards.
- Shipments are the cargo aggregate: billing client is set on the shipment itself, never inherited from a trip; ShipmentLegs reference trips by id only (no navigation into trips.trips).
- Route timetables live on RouteStop as per-leg OFFSET pairs (minutes after that leg's departure): Outbound/ReturnDepartureOffsetMinutes + Outbound/ReturnArrivalOffsetMinutes, inside the `stops` jsonb. The departure pair keeps the ORIGINAL jsonb keys OutboundOffsetMinutes/ReturnOffsetMinutes via the one shared Infrastructure/Persistence/RouteStopJsonMapping.Configure (routes, trips, rm_routes, rm_trips; pinned by RouteStopJsonMappingTests), so AddRouteStopArrivalOffsets is an empty migration. Null arrival = arrives when it departs. Offsets stay attached to their stop for the snapshot's life, including onto trips; the leg's TripDirection selects the pair, so every stop-list reversal copies ALL of them through unchanged — all reversals (ScheduleTripMaterializer, Trip.CreateDeadheadReturn, the Bookeo import, re-routing an Inbound leg, and CreateTripCommandHandler for an Inbound create) go through RouteStop.Reversed/OrientedFor. Route.Validate per leg: departures all-or-nothing, first stop 0, strictly increasing (outbound ascending Order, return descending); plus arrival rules ArrivalWithoutTimetable / ArrivalAtOrigin / ArrivalAfterDeparture / ArrivalBeforePreviousDeparture.
- Exact stop clock times are DERIVED at read time, never stored: Domain/Trips/StopTimetable.Resolve (direction selects the pair; untimed or non-ascending column → nulls; out-of-range arrival falls back to departure; never throws), surfaced as scheduledArrival/scheduledDeparture by TripStopResponse.From in TripReadService and the change-route preview.
- Schedule exceptions (special dates: skip / extra run / time override) are child rows of ScheduleTemplate, one per date, applied at generation time only — never to trips already materialized; past dates are allowed on purpose. Cargo-service templates normalize SeatsCapacity/SeatsMinimum to null (TripServiceTypeExtensions.IsCargoService decides).
- Integration/BookingDayConfirmedIntegrationEventHandler is the one handler here that arrives via RabbitMQ (chain-reaction), not outbox polling: Trip.ScheduleFromBooking creates the community trip (carries BookingDayId) and TripScheduledFromBooking flows back to Booking via the outbox.
- Re-routing is only Application/Trips/ChangeRoute (GET change-route/preview + POST change-route): the paired leg moves too only while Scheduled (else a PartnerNotChanged warning to acknowledge), manifests follow via TripManifest.RenameRoute, and a lost version token is TrySaveChangesAsync → ChangedConcurrently (409). PUT refuses a different routeId (UseChangeRoute) and on the same route keeps the trip's own snapshot rather than re-copying the catalogue.
- A trip becomes a deadhead (IsEmptyLeg) only via Application/Trips/ConvertToDeadhead (POST convert-to-deadhead, Scheduled only): refused while any manifest for it (by ManifestId AND by trip number) has passengers or cargo, it has seats confirmed or a gift-a-seat pledge, it is booking-sourced, a live Bookeo booking points at it, or its paired leg is already a deadhead; the empty manifests are deleted in the same save so a concurrent passenger add loses the version race (ChangedConcurrently). ConvertToPassengerTrip undoes it; PUT no longer carries IsEmptyLeg, and the Bookeo planner never targets a deadhead (TripIsDeadhead).
- Reopen (Application/Trips/Reopen, POST {id}/reopen, reason required, ≤500 chars): Trip.Reopen holds its own source → target map, deliberately NOT new CanTransition edges — Cancelled, InProgress, ReadyForBilling and WrittenOff ALL land in Scheduled (never InProgress, so the en-route gate runs again); Completed (paid) and Invoiced are refused. ReopenTripCommandHandler adds what the aggregate can't see: the optional ExpectedStatus (stale → 409 ReopenStatusChanged), ANY TripBilling replica claim refuses (that is how an invoice write-off is told apart from a dispatcher close-out, both WrittenOff), and a round-trip partner already claimed refuses (InProgress exempt) so one RoundTripKey group is never billed twice. Domain/Trips/Events/TripReopenedDomainEvent journals Reason plus the cancel/close-out reason it wiped (ClearedReason) and maps to Shared/IntegrationEvents/Trips/TripReopenedIntegrationEvent (trips.trip-reopened, outbox-polled; Billing is the only consumer).
- Trips/GetActivity reads `reason`, `clearedReason` (→ PreviousReason) and `enteredBy` generically from any trip event's payload, plus a server-composed Detail; when TripOperatorAccess.HasDispatchAccess is false (a driver) Reason/PreviousReason/Detail/EnteredBy are nulled on EVERY trip event, not just reopen. TripOperatorAccess is also the caller-owns-this-trip check that makes DriverAccess safe on /api/trips (the policy alone admits every driver).
- Domain/Planning/OperatingArea hard-codes Manitoba as the only operating area (owner decision, no toggle), enforced at every corridor write — Route.Create/Update, Trip.Schedule and its booking/import/deadhead siblings, Trip.Update, ChangeRoute; a stop with no recorded province counts as Manitoba.
<!-- notes:trips:end -->

<!-- notes:fleet:start -->
- Projections/FleetProjectionRegistry.cs is the single registry of every Fleet projection + same-module OnEvent reaction — DI (AddFleet) and the integration-test fixture both compose from it.
- MaintenancePlanDocumentMapping.cs holds the items/overhauls jsonb mapping shared by the maintenance_plans aggregate table and its rm_ read-model mirror, so write/read shapes can't drift.
- A defect has no id — it lives in the inspection's `defects` jsonb, so it is addressed by (InspectionId, Item) everywhere (Enter/Amend reject duplicate Items to keep that key unique); migration 20260912225642_AddDefectResolution is deliberately EMPTY because the resolution fields only change that jsonb payload.
- Resolution is final, never reopened: a returning fault is a NEW defect pointing back via RecurrenceOfInspectionId, Amend MERGES resolution stamps instead of replacing them, and manual resolve may not use the work-order-only reasons RepairedUnderWorkOrder/NoFaultFound (Recurrence itself is derived per read by VehicleDefectReadService, never stored).
- Work orders carry per-defect lines (`defects` jsonb, shared by work_orders + rm_work_orders via WorkOrderDefectLineMapping; migration AddWorkOrderDefectLines) linked back by InspectionDefect.WorkOrderId; completion applies each line's outcome — Repaired/NoFaultFound resolve, Deferred releases — while a legacy WO with no lines still resolves only the generating inspection's defects its line items name. VehicleInspection.IsHeldByWorkOrder (own WorkOrderId, or unresolved + open legacy GeneratedWorkOrderId) is THE rule both attach and Amend/remove use to refuse (DefectAlreadyOnWorkOrder / DefectOnActiveWorkOrder).
<!-- notes:fleet:end -->

- Application/Integration/UserLookup is a keyed replica of Identity accounts (upserted from UserChangedIntegrationEvent, never joined across modules) so a budget code can name its owner: FullName is the display value with Email as the always-present fallback, and the replica can never shrink because Identity.User is create-only.
- Vendors and CostCentres are TENANT-WIDE registers (budget codes are per period). Checks that need the register can't live on an aggregate, so they are Application rules — BudgetItemVendorRule, BudgetCodeCostCentreRule, CostCentreParentRule — and the *UsageProbe classes guard deletes; the by-vendor / by-cost-centre planned rollups are computed server-side (GetPlannedRollup slices).
- Qbo is a READ-ONLY QuickBooks Online link (expenses in, nothing out). No token may ever live on the QboConnection aggregate: tokens sit in Infrastructure/Qbo/QboTokenVault, a plain table on purpose (aggregates are snapshotted into append-only aggregate_snapshots, where a token could never be deleted), sealed by AesGcmQboTokenProtector under the env key Budgeting__QboTokenKey.
<!-- notes:budgeting:end -->

- /api/notifications requires the DispatchAccess policy (Owner/Dispatcher/Supervisor); send validates the template's service type + client pin against the trip (ServiceTypeMismatch/ClientMismatch in EmailTemplateErrors).
- {{PickupTime}}/{{DropoffTime}} resolve per recipient: PickupEmailRenderer prefers RecipientInput.PickupTime/DropoffTime and falls back to the command's trip-level ones (blank counts as absent). The times themselves are read from the trip's API-provided per-stop times (Dispatcher/lib/timetable.ts recipientTimes) — Notifications still never queries Trips; trip context stays an opaque snapshot composed by the dispatcher's screen.
- Integration/BookingDayRevertedIntegrationEventHandler is the module's first event-driven send (outbox-polled): "community trip at risk" emails to the event's recipient snapshot, built-in body unless an active CommunityBookingAtRisk template overrides; dispatch ids derive from EventId+chunk index so redelivery sends nothing twice.
- EmailDispatch is one row with THREE shapes: pickup (`Record`, trip+template), client accruals (`RecordClientAccruals`), and community booking passes (`RecordBookingPasses` — anchored on BookingId + BookingReference snapshot, trip/template/client all null; ServiceType CommunityBookingPasses). The passes email is HTML-only (no Quest PDF; BookingPassSheet arrives pre-formatted from the Dispatcher screen), SendBookingPassesEmail/BookingPassesRecipientGate delegates to AccrualsRecipientGate so the module keeps one regex/cap, and GET /emails history takes tripId > clientId > bookingId when several filters are supplied.
- Compliance alerts (driver out-of-service, ELD malfunction) go through Integration/ComplianceAlertMailer, addressed BY ROLE (e.g. ComplianceAccess ∪ DispatchAccess) and resolved to addresses via the module's own UserLookup replica of Identity; the alert's Kind is part of the deterministic dispatch id, so an "open" and its later "resolved" never collide.
<!-- notes:notifications:end -->

<!-- notes:billing:start -->
A QuickBooks prep worksheet, not an invoice system of record: the module prices completed
uninvoiced round trips per purchase order (PO rate, contract rate only as fallback; one draft per
PO, InvoiceDraftBuilder) and the numbers are keyed into QBO by hand (no QBO API call anywhere). It computes **no tax** — `Invoice.TotalCad` is the plain sum of its lines,
with no subtotal/GST split and no rate field; QuickBooks owns all tax calculation. Lifecycle is
Draft → EnteredInQbo → Paid (hand-confirmed, reversible), Void only off Draft, WrittenOff off
EnteredInQbo; no Sent/AR-aging.
- Integration/BillablePoolRemoval is the ONE "take a trip back out of the billable pool" rule, shared by the TripClosedWithoutBilling and TripReopened handlers: delete the uninvoiced billable_trips row (absence = not billable), keep with a warning a row an invoice already claims (the claim wins a race with Trips' reopen guard), absent row = idempotent no-op. A reopened trip finished again is re-added by TripReadyForBilling's insert-if-absent — nothing else needed.
<!-- notes:billing:end -->

- Corridors are a read-only replica of Trips routes (Integration/CorridorLookup, refreshed by RouteChangedIntegrationEventHandler via outbox polling) — Booking never references Trips. /api/booking requires DispatchAccess; the Settings/policy endpoints are AdminOnly.
- Persistence deliberately skips the rm_ read-model/projection pattern: read services query the aggregate tables directly, and all repository/read-service interfaces + impls are consolidated into single Repositories.cs / ReadServices.cs files (both in Abstractions/ and Persistence/).
- BookingDay lifecycle (Unconfirmed/Confirmed/Reverted): BookingDayThresholdService recomputes sold-vs-minimum INSIDE the confirm/cancel booking transaction and never saves itself; confirming publishes booking.booking-day-confirmed (the RabbitMQ chain-reaction event), reverting is gated by CancellationWindow + the Guarantee (Gift-a-Seat) flag.
- Domain/Bookings/BookingReference is the customer-facing NL-XXXXXX id (30-symbol alphabet without I/L/O/U/0/1) — immutable once stamped, the module's ONLY RNG (`Generate`), unique per tenant via the (tenant_id, reference) index with Create handler's collision guard in front; the AddBookingReference migration backfills existing rows inside a NO FORCE/FORCE RLS bracket. Bookings/GetById returns BookingDetailResponse = booking + its Customer row in one read (the detail screen's fetch and the create's Location target).
